To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding of a family 6 CBM from C. thermocellum to xylodextrins was enthalpy-driven and that the binding affinity and the enthalpy change of the binding were both dependent on the DP of the ligand.

the family 6 carbohydrate binding module of Clostridial thermocellum xynA binds to xyloligosaccharide with high affinity and the binding is enthalpy driven and that the binding is dependent on the length of the ligand.
the association constant of the CBM for xylooligosaccarides increased with increasing degree of polymerization, and that the binding was enthalpy-driven.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the binding of a family 6 CBM with xyloglucan, a major component of plant cell wall.
the binding of CBMs with xylooligo-saccharides, which may be useful in the development of new biofuels and biomaterials.

the binding of the C. thermocellum CBM with xylosides, and the results are consistent with the hypothesis that the CBM is involved in the recognition of the cellulosomal xylanase XynA with the substrate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of the family 6 CBM to xylooligosacharides is enthalpically driven, and the size of the binding site is 5 xylose residues long.
the binding of the family 6 CBM with xylans is an enthalpy-dominated reaction, and the size of the binding pocket is 5 xylose residues long.

the CBM of C. thermocellum xynA binds xylooligosacharides with high affinity and specificity, and that it has the ability to bind xylooligoscharides with DP 5 or more, which may be useful in industrial applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CBM of C. thermocellum is a good candidate as an affinity ligand in xylose purification.
the binding of the family 6 CBM with xylans is enthalpy driven and that the binding site size is about 5 xylose residues.
the CBM binds to the nonreducing terminus of the xylan chain and that the binding is driven by the formation of a large number of hydrophobic and hydrogen bonding interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of the family 6 CBM to the xylans is an enthalpy driven reaction, which can be attributed to the hydrophobic interactions.
the binding reaction of a CBM with xylose oligosaccharides is a highly enthalpy-driven process.
the CBM of C. thermocellum xylanase A has a binding affinity for xylooligosacharides with a DP of 5 or higher.
